new.title: Climb the keep of Thun Castle for the town view
new.desc: Thun Castle crowns the Schlossberg above the old town. Its keep houses a historical museum that has operated since 1888, and the tower gives views over the roofs, the Aare and the lake.
new.tip: Check hours first: the museum is open daily in spring and summer but only Sundays 1 to 4 pm from November to January.

new.title: Explore Spiez Castle and its lakeside church
new.desc: Schloss Spiez is a medieval castle on a hill above Lake Thun. Its museum covers about 1,300 years of local history, with rooms from the 13th to 18th centuries and a tower viewing platform.
new.tip: Church and gardens are free; the museum is open roughly Good Friday to mid-October, Tuesday to Sunday.

new.title: Stroll the gardens of Oberhofen Castle on the lake
new.desc: Schloss Oberhofen stands right on the shore of Lake Thun, with a medieval keep, a 15th-century palace and a 19th-century lake tower. It is a living museum with rooms furnished in styles from the 16th to 19th centuries, set in a large park.
new.tip: Park is free to enter; the museum runs from mid-May to mid-October (about 11 am to 5 pm). The boat landing is beside the castle.
new.q: Schloss Oberhofen, Staatsstrasse 2, 3653 Oberhofen am Thunersee

new.title: Walk the St. Beatus Caves and the dragon legend
new.desc: Show caves on Lake Thun in the Niederhorn massif, with over a kilometre of lit walkways, a cave museum and a legend of a dragon driven out by the monk Beatus in the 6th century.
new.tip: Guided tours last about 75 minutes. Open seasonally, so confirm dates at beatushoehlen.ch. There is a restaurant at the entrance.

new.title: See the 297 m Staubbach Falls in Lauterbrunnen
new.desc: Staubbach Falls drops 297 metres, one of the highest free-falling waterfalls in Europe, right by Lauterbrunnen village. The name means dust creek and the falls are said to have inspired Goethe.
new.tip: About five minutes on foot from the station. The Staubbach gallery behind the falls is open May to October; in winter the falls can freeze.

new.title: Follow the glacier waterfalls inside Trümmelbach Falls
new.desc: Ten glacier-fed waterfalls thunder inside the rock of the Lauterbrunnen valley, reached by a tunnel lift and walkways. The falls carry meltwater from the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau.
new.tip: Open early April to early November, daily 9 am to 5 pm (July and August from 8:30 am to 6 pm). Wear a jacket for the spray.

new.title: Ride the 1879 Giessbach funicular to the falls
new.desc: The Giessbach Falls cascade down 14 steps above Lake Brienz, and a path leads behind the water. The Giessbachbahn, running since 1879, is one of Europe's oldest funiculars and a mechanical engineering landmark.
new.tip: Take the boat to the Giessbach landing and ride the funicular up to the Grandhotel. Service is mainly April to October.

new.title: Wander the historic houses of Ballenberg
new.desc: Ballenberg is the Swiss open-air museum near Brienz, with farmhouses and workshops moved from all regions of the country, plus traditional crafts and farm animals.
new.tip: Open mid-April to late October or early November, 10 am to 5 pm. Allow a full day and use the two entrances at Hofstetten and Brienz.
new.q: Freilichtmuseum Ballenberg, Museumstrasse 131, 3858 Hofstetten bei Brienz

new.title: Walk the walkways of the Aare Gorge
new.desc: The Aare cut a limestone gorge near Meiringen, and a walkway clings to the rock face with tunnels and galleries. The gorge has two entrances, west and east.
new.tip: Open about April to early November, daily from 8:30 am; the west entrance opens earlier than the east.

new.title: Ride the Reichenbach funicular to Holmes's falls
new.desc: The Reichenbach Falls tumble about 110 metres above Meiringen and are where Conan Doyle's 1893 story The Final Problem has Holmes and Moriarty fall. The funicular has climbed to the falls since 1899.
new.tip: The funicular runs seasonally (roughly May to October); a combined ticket with the Sherlock Holmes Museum is sold. Hiking up from the valley is also possible.

new.title: Visit Oeschinensee by gondola from Kandersteg
new.desc: Oeschinensee is a high-alpine lake at about 1,578 m beneath the Blüemlisalp massif. The gondola from Kandersteg reaches a mountain station, from where a walk of about 30 minutes leads down to the shore.
new.tip: Book the gondola time slot online in summer. A summer toboggan run sits next to the upper station and rowboats are for hire.

new.title: Ride the Jungfrau railway to the Top of Europe
new.desc: The Jungfraujoch saddle at 3,454 m is reached by train through the Eiger and Mönch. The site includes the Sphinx observatory at 3,571 m, completed in 1937, with a viewing deck.
new.tip: Book early and check the webcam; fog can ruin the view. Tickets are expensive, and Swiss and Jungfrau passes give discounts.
new.q: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe, Jungfraujoch, 3801 Grindelwald

new.title: Ride to Piz Gloria on the Schilthorn
new.desc: The Schilthorn summit (2,970 m) holds the revolving restaurant Piz Gloria, used in the 1969 James Bond film On Her Majesty's Secret Service. Cable cars run from Stechelberg through Mürren and Birg, including the world's steepest section.
new.tip: Open all year; check weather first. A return from Mürren costs less than from Stechelberg, and the Bond World exhibition is at the top.

new.title: Cross the Glacier Canyon boardwalks near Grindelwald
new.desc: The Gletscherschlucht is a gorge cut by meltwater from the Lower Grindelwald Glacier, with a walkway about 1 km long through rock galleries and tunnels. A crystal museum and cafe are at the exit.
new.tip: Open about May to November, usually from around 9:30 am. Bus 122 from Grindelwald station goes to the entrance.

new.title: Step onto the Two Lakes Bridge at Harder Kulm
new.desc: The Harder funicular climbs 755 m from Interlaken Ost in about ten minutes. At the top the glazed Zwei-Seen-Steg platform looks over lakes Thun and Brienz and the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau.
new.tip: Funicular runs from April to end of November (2026: 3 April to 29 November), with evening trips in summer.

new.title: Photograph Seeburg castle on the Iseltwald peninsula
new.desc: Iseltwald is a small village on Lake Brienz, known for Seeburg, a lakeside castle on a peninsula. It is viewed from the water or from paths such as the Farnihubel viewpoint, as it is not open to visitors.
new.tip: Reach it by lake boat from Interlaken or Brienz, or walk the shore path from Giessbach.

new.title: Visit the Sherlock Holmes Museum in Meiringen
new.desc: The small museum on Conan Doyle Place opened in 1991 and shows Victorian-era items and a replica of the 221B Baker Street sitting room. A statue of Holmes stands outside.
new.tip: Opening hours are reduced outside May to October; check sherlockholmes.ch. Combined tickets with the funicular exist.
new.q: Sherlock Holmes Museum, Conan Doyle Place, 3860 Meiringen

new.title: See the Engstligen Falls above Adelboden
new.desc: The Engstligen Falls drop about 600 m and are described as the second-highest waterfall in Switzerland. The cable car to Engstligenalp passes the falls, and the plateau above has mountain restaurants.
new.tip: Walking from Adelboden takes about 1.5 hours. The plateau is also a winter destination.

new.title: Walk through Blausee nature park and its trout ponds
new.desc: Blausee is a small clear lake in a car-free park of about 20 hectares near Kandersteg, with an organic trout farm, forest paths and a lakeside restaurant serving the trout.
new.tip: Entry fee includes the trout ponds. Check blausee.ch for hours, as parts close for maintenance in winter.

new.title: Walk Thun's two-level Obere Hauptgasse
new.desc: Thun's old town has a main street with raised pavements on two levels, shops on the upper tier and views up to the castle. Rathausplatz, the historic centre, hosts a Saturday market.
new.tip: Continue to Mühleplatz for restaurants and bars, and go up the covered stairs to the castle.

new.title: Visit Brienz, Switzerland's woodcarving capital
new.desc: The village on Lake Brienz is home to Switzerland's only woodcarving school, founded in 1884, and the Swiss Woodcarving Museum, founded in 2009. Visitors can watch students at work in the showroom.
new.tip: The museum is open Wednesday to Sunday afternoons from about May to October, and the school showroom has its own hours.
new.q: Museum der Holzbildhauerei, Brienz BE, 3855 Brienz

new.title: Cross the Sigriswil Panoramabrücke over Gummischlucht
new.desc: A 340 m steel suspension bridge spans the 182 m deep Gummi gorge between Sigriswil and Aeschlen, with views of Lake Thun and the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau.
new.tip: Open all year, with a modest day fee. Bus 25 runs from Thun station to Sigriswil.

new.title: See the Thun-Panorama of 1814 at Schadaupark
new.desc: Schloss Schadau (1846 to 1854, Gothic Revival) stands in a park on Lake Thun. Next to it a rotunda houses the 38 m Thun-Panorama painted by Marquard Wocher in 1809 to 1814, regarded as the oldest surviving panorama painting.
new.tip: The park is free; check thun-panorama.com for museum hours.

new.title: Look at the Jungfrau from Interlaken's Höhematte
new.desc: The Höhematte is the central meadow of Interlaken between Höheweg and Jungfraustrasse, protected since 1864, and the main landing field for paragliders with a classic view of the Jungfrau.
new.tip: Walk along the Höheweg promenade past the Victoria-Jungfrau hotel for the best view.

new.title: Cruise Lake Thun on the paddle steamer Blümlisalp
new.desc: The Blümlisalp, built in 1906, is a paddle steamer that BLS runs on Lake Thun between April and October after a restoration that brought it back in 1992.
new.tip: Boats leave from the Thun jetty; check the BLS timetable, since the steamer does not sail every day.

new.title: Ride the steam cog railway up the Brienzer Rothorn
new.desc: The Brienz Rothorn Railway has run since 1892 and is a steam rack railway of about 7.6 km, climbing for about an hour past eight tunnels to the summit area at 2,244 m.
new.tip: The 2026 season ran 6 June to 25 October; book a seat guarantee in summer as trains can sell out.

new.title: Step out on the First Cliff Walk above Grindelwald
new.desc: A cliffside walkway at around 2,166 m on First, reached by gondola from Grindelwald, with a viewing platform over a drop. Next door the First Flyer zipline runs 800 m to Schreckfeld.
new.tip: The cliff walk is free once you hold a gondola ticket; the gondola ride takes about 25 minutes.
new.q: First Cliff Walk by Tissot, First, 3818 Grindelwald

new.title: Hike from First to the Bachalpsee mirror lake
new.desc: An easy, mostly flat walk of about an hour each way from the First gondola station to the Bachalpsee, a lake at 2,265 m.
new.tip: Buy a gondola ticket to First. The path continues to the Faulhorn for a longer day.

new.title: Ride the 1893 cog railway to Schynige Platte
new.desc: A cog railway has run from Wilderswil to Schynige Platte since 1893, taking about 52 minutes. At the top an alpine botanical garden shows around 600 species.
new.tip: Runs about late May to October; check the timetable.

new.title: Walk the Männlichen to Kleine Scheidegg panorama trail
new.desc: A ridge path of about 4.5 to 6 km with views of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. It is mostly easy and downhill, and the Wengernalp Railway can take you from Kleine Scheidegg back to Wengen.
new.tip: Take the Wengen to Männlichen cable car. Allow about 1.5 hours.

new.title: Hike the Faulhornweg from Schynige Platte to First
new.desc: A long day hike of about 15 to 16 km and 6 hours via the Faulhorn summit at 2,680 m, with views of Lake Thun and Lake Brienz, passing Bachalpsee before ending at First.
new.tip: Hike in summer and check trail conditions. You can split it with a night at the Faulhorn hotel.

new.title: Ride the Niesenbahn funicular to the Niesen summit
new.desc: The Niesenbahn climbs 3.5 km in two sections from Mülenen to Niesen Kulm at 2,336 m, opened in 1910, and takes about 30 minutes in total.
new.tip: Runs daily from end of April to mid-November. The valley station is 4 minutes from Mülenen station.

new.title: Take the Allmendhubel funicular and flower trail
new.desc: A four-minute funicular from Mürren to a 1,907 m viewpoint with a flower trail and a children's playground. The flower trail runs about 2 km back down to Mürren.
new.tip: Operates in summer from about mid-June to mid-October, with revision breaks, so check before going.

new.title: Ride up to the Niederhorn above Lake Thun
new.desc: A funicular from Beatenbucht to Beatenberg and a cable car carry visitors to the Niederhorn summit with a panorama of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau and lake views.
new.tip: The funicular runs all year; the cable car is seasonal, and one listing notes a technical suspension, so check niederhorn.ch.

new.title: Fly a tandem paraglider over Interlaken
new.desc: Skywings runs tandem flights from Beatenberg, landing in Interlaken, with pickup from town included. No experience is needed.
new.tip: Weight limits of about 80 to 90 kg apply, and flights are year-round but weather dependent.

new.title: Take a lake boat from Interlaken Ost to Giessbach and Iseltwald
new.desc: Boats on Lake Brienz run from Interlaken Ost past Iseltwald and the Giessbach Falls to Brienz, calling at Oberried and Niederried.
new.tip: Season is about mid-April to mid-October. Day passes are sold, and you can hop off at Giessbach or Iseltwald.

new.title: Ride the Gelmerbahn, Europe's steepest open funicular
new.desc: The Gelmerbahn climbs from Handeck to the Gelmersee at about 1,850 m, with a maximum gradient of 106 percent and a rattling 12-minute ride.
new.tip: The season is about May to October. Buy tickets online; dam access was restricted in summer 2026.

new.title: Hike the Gasterntal from Kandersteg
new.desc: The Gasterntal is a wild glacial valley south of Kandersteg, walked from Sunnbüel to Selden along the Kander. The easy version is about 8.9 km in 3 hours.
new.tip: The bus from Selden to Kandersteg runs June to October and must be reserved. Hotel Waldhaus and Berghotel Gasterntal are on the way.

new.title: Walk the valley path from Lenk to the Simmen Falls
new.desc: A level walk of about 5.3 km (about 1 hour 20 minutes) leads from Lenk to the Simmenfälle, where the Simme river cascades. The Seven Springs are a nearby karst spring on longer routes.
new.tip: The official season is June to October. Buses return to Lenk.

new.title: Swim at the Schwäbis river pool on the Aare
new.desc: The Schwäbis is Thun's river pool, with bathing since 1884, separate swimmer and non-swimmer areas, a slide and a sandpit. Rafting and float trips to Bern start here.
new.tip: Open daily May to September. The current is strong, so only confident swimmers should go in the main river.

new.title: Hike the Eiger Trail below the north face
new.desc: A gravel path of about 6 km along the foot of the Eiger north face between Eigergletscher and Alpiglen, rated moderate, with a short uphill section. The north face was first climbed in 1938.
new.tip: Reach Eigergletscher by train and finish at Alpiglen. Bring food and water as there is none between.

new.title: Watch the Lauberhorn downhill at the Hundschopf in Wengen
new.desc: The Lauberhorn races in Wengen began in 1930 and the downhill is 4.48 km, the longest on the World Cup circuit. The Hundschopf is a jump about a third of the way down.
new.tip: Held in mid-January. Wengen is car-free, reached by train from Lauterbrunnen.

new.title: Walk the Gstaad Promenade and village loop
new.desc: The Promenade is Gstaad's short pedestrian street, with a village loop past the Gstaad Palace and the 1905 railway viaduct and on through Mettlenwald.
new.tip: The loop takes about an hour. Guided village tours run on Fridays at 10 am.

new.title: Order house torte and pralines at Grand Café Schuh
new.desc: Grand Café Restaurant Schuh on the Höheweg is a confiserie, café and restaurant that has sold chocolate and coffee since 1818 and serves Swiss dishes, fondue and pastries.
new.tip: Take a slice of torte or pralines with coffee on the large terrace; open daily, later on weekdays.
new.q: Grand Café Restaurant Schuh, Höheweg 56, 3800 Interlaken

new.title: Eat raclette in the 18th-century Landgasthof Ruedihus
new.desc: A restored 18th-century chalet inn on the edge of Kandersteg, with painted panelling, serving regional dishes such as raclette and fondue.
new.tip: Opposite the Waldhotel Doldenhorn; book ahead for dinner.

new.title: Eat Lake Brienz fish at Elisa at Giessbach
new.desc: The Grandhotel Giessbach's bistro Elisa serves fish from Lake Brienz and vegetables from the hotel's 2 hectare garden, on a terrace above the lake and falls.
new.tip: Open spring to autumn, lunch and dinner. Reach it by boat and funicular.
new.q: Elisa Bistro & Terrasse, Grandhotel Giessbach, 3855 Brienz

new.title: Have cheese fondue at La Fromagerie in Gstaad Palace
new.desc: The fondue restaurant of the Gstaad Palace sits in a bunker where a Swiss bank stored gold in the Second World War, and is the hotel's most popular restaurant.
new.tip: Reserve ahead; it is an upmarket hotel experience.
new.q: La Fromagerie, Gstaad Palace, Palacestrasse 28, 3780 Gstaad

new.title: Buy Thunfischli almond cakes at Confiserie Steinmann
new.desc: Confiserie Tea Room Steinmann in Thun's Bälliz has made hand-decorated truffles and pastries since 1920 and serves coffee creations and lunch. Local guides point to the Thunfischli and Thunerli as local sweets.
new.tip: Closed on Sundays per one listing.
new.q: Confiserie Tea Room Steinmann, Bälliz 37, 3600 Thun

new.title: Order the Röstizza at Kleine Scheidegg
new.desc: The Bergrestaurant Kleine Scheidegg at 2,061 m has a terrace facing the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. Its signature dish is the Röstizza, a rösti pizza.
new.tip: Reach it by Wengernalp or Jungfrau Railway; the terrace is best in sun.
new.q: Bergrestaurant Kleine Scheidegg, Kleine Scheidegg, 3801 Grindelwald

new.title: Eat fondue at the Stägerstübli in Mürren
new.desc: A cosy chalet restaurant in Mürren, a locals' haunt, with a terrace, serving Swiss dishes, fondue and raclette.
new.tip: Warm kitchen from about 11:30 to 20:30.

new.title: Try lake fish at Seerestaurant Löwen in Brienz
new.desc: A lakeside restaurant in Brienz with about 70 indoor seats and a 110-seat terrace, listing fish specialties among its dishes.
new.tip: Closed from mid-October to mid-March except for the Brienz Christmas market.

new.title: Dine on the terrace of Schloss Schadau in Thun
new.desc: The restaurant of Schloss Schadau serves modern French-Mediterranean dishes with a lake-view terrace in Schadaupark, in a Gothic Revival castle.
new.tip: Open from morning to late evening; book for dinner.

new.title: Taste local beer at the Rugenbräu brewery in Matten
new.desc: Rugenbräu is the Interlaken-area brewery in Matten, offering brewery and distillery tours and supplying the Hüsi Pub in town.
new.tip: Tours may require advance booking and may be in German; check first.
new.q: Rugenbräu AG, Wagnerenstrasse 40, 3800 Matten bei Interlaken

new.title: Order truffle fondue at Le Petit Chalet in Gstaad
new.desc: A small old-fashioned fondue spot in the gardens of Le Grand Bellevue, known for truffle fondue, goat cheese fondue and raclette.
new.tip: Book ahead in winter.
new.q: Le Petit Chalet, Le Grand Bellevue, Untergstaadstrasse 17, 3780 Gstaad

new.title: Eat bratwurst with rösti at Berghaus Alpiglen
new.desc: Berghaus Alpiglen sits directly beneath the Eiger north face and serves homemade bratwurst with rösti, with a children's playground.
new.tip: Reach it by Wengernalp railway and combine with the Eiger Trail.
